oneOf.description: Terminate sessions on the source database, then clone (bounded retries).
Refuse to clone a source database that has sessions.
Wait up to `busy_wait` for the sessions to end, then refuse naming them.

CowCapability.description: Whether cloned databases share blocks with their source.

oneOf.description: Block sharing was verified on the server's data directory.
Clones are full copies.
Not verifiable from here (external servers).

DataSection.description:
`[data]`: seed data for runs that cannot prompt.

"Non-interactive" is a run that cannot ask: `--non-interactive`, `--json`, no terminal, the Git hook. Such a run that was not told where the data comes from (`--data-from`) takes it from here, for every service that has a snapshot of that name, and from the service's usual default (with a warning) for one that does not.

The section decides where the data of a workspace comes from when it is created or adopted. A data source is immutable once chosen, so it is part of no generation: changing it reopens no workspace that has its data.

noninteractive_fallback.description: What a service without that snapshot does. Unset, it fails the run (with remedies): its default data source is a live workspace, and cloning one ends PostgreSQL sessions or stops MySQL. The only value is `"empty"`: an empty database for that service, with a warning.

noninteractive_from.description: `snapshot:NAME` (or `snapshot:NAME@vN`): the snapshot each service seeds a non-interactive workspace from.

noninteractive_max_age.description: A seed snapshot older than this (humantime, e.g. "7d") is still used, with a warning.

EnvPreset.description: A framework preset: a fixed set of variables rendered from the PostgreSQL binding's connection parameters.

oneOf.description: `DIRECT_URL` (the same URL). `SHADOW_DATABASE_URL` comes with a `shadow` scratch database (`extra_databases = ["shadow"]`): devflow exports it itself, with the other scratch URLs, so Prisma's `shadowDatabaseUrl = env("SHADOW_DATABASE_URL")` finds it whether or not this preset is on.
`DB_CONNECTION`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`.
`SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` (JDBC), `_USERNAME`, `_PASSWORD`.
`SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI` (`postgresql+psycopg://`).
`DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`.

additionalProperties.description: A recipe: the value template of the variable named by the key. `${NAME}` references a variable devflow generates.

EnvSection.description: Extra variables for `.devflow/env`: `NAME = "value"` recipes built from the variables devflow generates (`${DATABASE_URL}`, `${PGHOST}`, …, one pass, no defaults, never another recipe), and framework presets. Recipes and presets are part of what `devflow trust` approves.

presets.description: Framework presets rendered from the PostgreSQL connection. A preset cannot set a name that a recipe or another preset sets.

GitHookMode.description: When the post-checkout hook's setup runs relative to Git.

oneOf.description: Git waits for the whole setup (4.3 s for a 4 s hook): the worktree is ready when `git worktree add` returns.

`git worktree add` returns at once; the setup runs detached (its own process group, log in the worktree's Git directory). Whoever needs the workspace waits for it (`devflow wait`, `devflow setup --wait`, `devflow exec --wait`).

name.description: Shown in logs and output; unique within the phase.

timeout.description: Overrides `[hooks] timeout` for this command (a duration such as "30s" or "5m").

HookEntry.description: One hook command, run with `sh -c` (no templating): a string, or a table when it deserves a name in logs and output or a timeout of its own.

setup.description: Run once in a new (or adopted) worktree, after payloads, database and env.

switch.description: Run on every `devflow switch` into an existing workspace.

teardown.description: Run before removal; a failure blocks removal unless forced.

timeout.description: Per-command timeout (humantime, e.g. "15m"); an entry's own `timeout` overrides it.

IntegrationsSection.description:
`[integrations]`: the Git hook and the agent hosts.

Nothing here decides what a workspace holds, so it is part of no generation and of no approval: it only changes when the post-checkout hook returns.

git_hook.description: What the post-checkout hook does after `git worktree add`: set the worktree up before Git returns (`"synchronous"`, the default), or start the setup detached and return at once (`"background"`).

PitchforkSection.description: `[pitchfork]`: devflow's part in starting a workspace's daemons.

autostart.description: Start the workspace's daemons once it is `ready` after `setup` and `switch` (and when switching into a ready one). Chosen at onboarding; off by default. Starting is still gated by the approval of the workspace's pitchfork configuration, and never happens while a daemon starts on its own (`cron`, `watch`, `boot_start`, `auto`).

oneOf.description: devflow runs a PostgreSQL container with `docker compose`.
An existing PostgreSQL ≥ 18 server reached through `admin_url`.

id.description: Stable across machines; written by `devflow init` and committed.

SeedFallback.description: What `[data] noninteractive_fallback` allows a service without the seed snapshot to start from.

oneOf.description: An empty database (an empty cache, an initialized MySQL).

ServiceConfig.description:
One `[services.<key>]` table, selected by its `engine`.

Internally tagged: `engine = "postgres"` plus the engine's own keys, which stay strict (`deny_unknown_fields` on the section).

admin_url.description: External mode: admin (provisioner) connection URL. `DEVFLOW_PG_ADMIN_URL` overrides it.

app_host.description: Host written into workspace URLs when it differs from the admin endpoint.

app_port.description: Port written into workspace URLs when it differs from the admin endpoint.

bind.description: Managed mode: address the container port is published on.

busy_wait.description: With `on_busy_source = "wait"`: how long to wait for the source's sessions to end (humantime). Default: `30s`.

cow.description: External mode: operator declaration after checking the server's filesystem.

database.description: Display name of the default workspace's database branch.

extra_databases.description: Scratch databases every branch gets besides its own (`["test", "shadow"]`): empty, recorded, owned like the branch's data and reachable with the branch's login. Each is exported as `<NAME>_DATABASE_URL`. Each name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or `_` (21 characters at most), listed once, and not main, postgres, devflow or template*.

image.description: Managed mode: image to run; must be PostgreSQL ≥ 18.

on_busy_source.description: Default: `disconnect` for a managed server bound to loopback, `fail` otherwise.

port.description: Managed mode: fixed host port; 0 (the default) lets devflow choose one and keep it, recorded in the server's `admin.json`.

require_cow.description: Refuse to create branches unless CoW is verified.

wal_log_below.description: A clone of a source smaller than this uses `STRATEGY WAL_LOG` unless copy-on-write is verified (a size like "256MiB"; "0" always uses `FILE_COPY`). Default: `256MiB`.

oneOf.description: The keys of a `valkey`, `redis` or `mysql` service. Container engines are managed only: devflow runs the containers, so there is no `mode`, `admin_url` or port to configure (each branch's host port is allocated once and kept).

env.description: Variable the connection URL is exported as. Default: `REDIS_URL` for `valkey` and `redis`; for `mysql` `DATABASE_URL`, or `MYSQL_URL` when the project also has a postgres service.

image.description: Image to run, by tag or digest. Default: `valkey/valkey:8-alpine`, `redis:8-alpine` or `mysql:8.4`. A branch pins the image digest it was created with.

require_cow.description: Refuse to clone unless the filesystem shares blocks (reflink); without it a full copy is allowed and reported as `copy`.

oneOf.description: The keys of a `valkey`, `redis` or `mysql` service. Container engines are managed only: devflow runs the containers, so there is no `mode`, `admin_url` or port to configure (each branch's host port is allocated once and kept).

database.description: `mysql` only: the database every branch of the service has (the schema its application account owns). Default: the project name as an identifier. Branches cloned from existing data keep the name that data has.

env.description: Variable the connection URL is exported as. Default: `REDIS_URL` for `valkey` and `redis`; for `mysql` `DATABASE_URL`, or `MYSQL_URL` when the project also has a postgres service.

oneOf.title: mysql

oneOf.description: The keys of a `sqlite` service. The database is a file in the workspace: nothing runs and nothing is configured about a server, a port or an image.

busy_wait.description: How long a clone waits for a writer to release the source file (humantime, e.g. "30s"); then it is refused rather than copied while it changes. Default: `30s`.

env.description: Variable the `sqlite:` URL of the file is exported as. Default: `DATABASE_URL`, or `SQLITE_URL` when another service claims `DATABASE_URL` (a postgres service, or a mysql service without an `env` of its own when there is no postgres service).

path.description: The database file, relative to the worktree (`db/development.sqlite3`). Each workspace has its own, at the same relative path: a workspace's file is cloned from its source's when the workspace is set up. The file need not exist yet in a project that has not created it.

path_env.description: Variable the absolute path of the file is exported as. Default: `SQLITE_PATH`. Recipes can build any other form from it (`sqlite:///${SQLITE_PATH}` for SQLAlchemy, `file:${SQLITE_PATH}` for Prisma).

require_cow.description: Refuse to clone unless the file system shares blocks (reflink); without it a full copy is allowed and reported as `copy`.

oneOf.title: sqlite

checkout.description: Machine-local: only devflow.local.toml may set it (it chooses who checks worktrees out, and `git` authorizes Git's own filters and hooks), so a committed file that sets it is a configuration error.

copy.description: Paths cloned from the source worktree into new worktrees when present.

dir.description: Parent directory for new worktrees, relative to the main checkout. `{project}` and `{repo}` expand to the project name and the main checkout's directory name.

focus_ports.description: The loopback ports `devflow focus` forwards to the focused workspace when none is named (an OAuth callback registered for `http://localhost:3000`, say).

port_range.description: The ports `DEVFLOW_PORT` is chosen from, `[first, last]` inclusive, with 1024 <= first <= last <= 65535 (default `[40000, 49999]`). A port a workspace already has is kept whatever this says now.

description: devflow 1.0 project configuration (devflow.toml or .devflow.toml), committed at the repository root. Generated from the configuration types by `devflow config schema`; a document can pass it and still be refused (durations, at most one postgres and one mysql service, two services exporting one variable, `${NAME}` references).

data.description: Where the data of workspaces nobody can be asked about comes from.

env.description: Extra variables for `.devflow/env`: recipes built from devflow's own variables, and framework presets.

hooks.description: Shell commands (`sh -c`) run in a workspace, gated by `devflow trust`. Write them so that running them twice is safe.

integrations.description: How devflow works with the tools that create worktrees.

pitchfork.description: How devflow treats the project's pitchfork daemons.

project.description: The project's identity: its name and the id that ties trust, the registry and the database server to it across machines.

services.description: Services by key (`[services.db]`), each selected by its `engine`. The key names the service in receipts and output: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`, at most 31 characters (a container or sqlite service cannot be named status, up, down, url, list, snapshot, reset, reconcile, forget, help). At most one `postgres` and one `mysql` service.

worktree.description: Where new worktrees go and what they take with them.
